findings.title: Federated recovery credentials permanently shadow locally generated replacements
findings.body: The helper always returns a federated/user-storage recovery credential when one exists and only considers the local credential when none exists. However, `createRecoveryCodesCredential` falls back to local storage whenever a user-storage provider returns `false` from `updateCredential` (for example, a read-only provider). If that provider already exposes an older recovery-code credential, a recovery-code reset creates and displays a new local set, but this helper continues to use the old federated credential for the code-number display and all-codes-used/required-action handling. This makes recovery-code regeneration inconsistent and can leave the user unable to complete the expected reconfiguration flow. The fallback must either replace/disable the old federated credential, avoid creating a local credential while a federated one remains authoritative, or use an unambiguous precedence mechanism.

findings.title: Recovery credential enumeration returns a different credential ID than the stored credential
findings.body: `recoveryCodesModel` is rebuilt with `createFromValues`, which has no input for the ID assigned at line 195, so the credential returned by `getCredentials` cannot retain `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`. Consumers use the enumerated ID to remove credentials; in particular the recovery-code authenticator calls `removeStoredCredentialById` after all codes are consumed. Consequently this test storage cannot exercise removal of the actual stored recovery credential, and account/API credential operations may target an unknown ID. Preserve the original credential ID (and other persisted metadata) on the model returned by `getCredentials`.

findings.title: Test user storage validates recovery codes without consuming them
findings.body: The recovery-code validator accepts any matching generated code but never marks the matching code as used or persists an updated credential. Recovery authentication codes are one-time credentials; this provider therefore permits indefinite replay of every code. The new integration test logs in with only one code and does not attempt a replay or consume all codes, so it passes despite this broken behavior and does not verify the all-codes-used path. Update the provider/test fixture to persist code consumption and add replay/exhaustion assertions.
